paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a portfolio of novel and proprietary molecular glue degraders, or MGDs. MGDs are small molecule drugs that employ the body's natural protein destruction mechanisms to selectively degrade therapeutically relevant proteins, in effect editing the human proteome. MGDs function by inducing the engagement of an E3 ligase, such as cereblon, with defined structural features on surfaces of target proteins. These target proteins are also referred to as neosubstrates. The E3 ligase then tags the target protein for degradation by adding a molecular mark known as ubiquitin. We believe our MGDs provide significant advantages over existing therapeutic modalities, including other protein degradation approaches.

We have developed a proprietary and industry leading discovery engine, called QuEENTM (an abbreviation for "Quantitative and Engineered Elimination of Neosubstrates") to enable our unique target-centric MGD discovery and development approach and our rational design of MGD product candidates.

To date, our QuEENTM discovery engine has identified numerous proteins for potential targeting by our MGDs, including those targeted by product candidates in our pipeline. We combine our artificial intelligence or "AI" / machine learning or "ML" engines with multiple proprietary experimental tools to identify therapeutically relevant target proteins amenable to degradation by our MGDs. We are continuously increasing our understanding of how MGDs function and we are using this understanding to develop design principles for the engineering of new MGDs. This growing expertise manifests in our expanding MGD library as well as our discovery and development pipeline. Using our insights, knowhow, and technology platform we have generated a library of MGDs that forms the basis for our MGD programs. At present, our library comprises a diverse set of rationally designed small molecules representing more than 1000 unique low molecular weight scaffolds and over 75,000 different MGD molecules. We also use our insights and learnings to continuously update and improve QuEENTM and our MGD library, consistently increasing the power of the discovery engine.

We prioritize our product development to address therapeutic targets backed by strong biological and genetic rationales. We are focused on developing solutions to clinically important indications, including indications in immunology, inflammation, cardiology, oncology, and others. To date, our discovery engine has resulted in three programs in clinical development: MRT-6160, a VAV1-directed MGD for immune-mediated diseases; MRT-8102, a NEK7-directed MGD for inflammatory diseases driven by IL-1β, IL-6, and the NLRP3 inflammasome; and MRT-2359, a GSPT1-directed MGD for metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC).

MRT-6160 is a VAV1-directed MGD being developed for immune-mediated diseases. Our preclinical studies showed that targeted degradation of VAV1 protein via an MGD modulates both T- and B-cell receptor activity. Our VAV1 MGD, MRT-6160, showed promising activity in preclinical models of neurologic and systemic autoimmune and inflammatory diseases and thus we believe has the potential to provide therapeutic benefit in multiple immune-mediated diseases, such as inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, dermatological disorders, and multiple sclerosis.

In October 2024, we announced a global exclusive development and commercialization license agreement with Novartis under which we granted to Novartis an exclusive license to develop, manufacture, and commercialize VAV1-directed MGDs including MRT-6160, starting with Phase 2 clinical studies. We received from Novartis an upfront payment of $150 million and are eligible to receive up to $2.1 billion in development, regulatory, and sales milestones, beginning upon initiation of Phase 2 studies and including potential development and regulatory milestone payments, exceeding $1.5 billion if multiple indications achieve regulatory approval in multiple territories. We and Novartis also agreed to a net profit and loss sharing arrangement, in which we will co-fund any global clinical development from Phase 3 onwards and will share 30% of any profits and losses associated with the manufacturing and commercialization of the licensed products in the United States. We are eligible to receive from Novartis potential sales milestone payments and tiered royalties in connection with sales outside of the United States. We were responsible for costs associated with the now completed Phase 1 clinical study and Novartis will be responsible for costs associated with any subsequent clinical studies except for the Phase 3 costs covered by us under the profit and loss sharing agreement.

In March 2025, we announced initial clinical results from our Phase 1 study of MRT-6160, demonstrating deep VAV1 degradation of greater than 90%, significant T and B cell functional inhibition, including profound inhibition

of cytokine release from T and B cells ex-vivo, and a generally favorable safety and tolerability profile. We believe these data support a clear path to multiple Phase 2 studies and broad potential applications in immune-mediated diseases. We expect that our collaborator, Novartis, will initiate multiple Phase 2 studies of MRT-6160 in immune-mediated diseases in 2026.

MRT-8102 is a NEK7-directed MGD targeting diseases and inflammatory conditions driven by the NLRP3 inflammasome, IL-1, and IL-6. The NLRP3 inflammasome is a multi-protein complex that serves as a central node for integrating signals from pathogens, damage, and stress, and triggers the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Aberrant NLRP3 inflammasome activation and the subsequent release of active interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and interleukin-18 (IL-18) have been implicated in multiple inflammation-driven diseases, including atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), gout, hidradenitis suppurativa, pericarditis, osteoarthritis, and obesity. NEK7, functioning as a scaffolding protein, facilitates assembly and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in a kinase-independent manner, suggesting that degradation of NEK7 with an MGD molecule would be a potentially attractive therapeutic approach to preventing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and associated downstream cytokine production.

In January 2026, we announced positive interim data from an ongoing Phase 1 clinical study (now called GFORCE-1) evaluating MRT-8102. In subjects with elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, MRT-8102 demonstrated rapid and durable reductions in systemic inflammation. After four weeks of MRT-8102 treatment in subjects with elevated CVD risk, C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were reduced by 85%, and 94% of study participants achieved CRP values below 2 mg/L, a threshold associated with reduced CVD risk. The single ascending dose (SAD) and multiple ascending dose (MAD) cohorts demonstrated deep and sustained NEK7 degradation at doses from 5 mg to 400 mg. A favorable safety profile was observed with mild to moderate adverse events (AEs) and no evidence of increased infection risk.

Our ongoing GFORCE-1 Study of MRT-8102 in subjects with elevated CVD risk has been expanded to multiple dose levels to accelerate development in ASCVD. We anticipate results from this study in H2 2026. We plan to initiate a Phase 2 ASCVD study, GFORCE-2, (in elevated CVD risk patients defined by Stage 3/4 chronic kidney disease and elevated CRP) in H2 2026, a Phase 2 study of MRT-8102 in patients with gout flares, GFORCE-3, in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027, and a Phase 2 study in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa, GFORCE-4, in H1 2027. Furthermore, we expect to submit an IND application for a next-generation NEK7-directed MGD in 2026.

MRT-2359 is an orally bioavailable MGD targeting the translation termination factor protein GSPT1 and is currently in clinical development for potential use in MYC-driven tumors, with a focus on metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, or mCRPC. GSPT1 (also known as eRF3a) is a translation termination factor that helps catalyze the termination of protein synthesis, facilitating the release of mRNA and newly synthesized protein from the ribosomal protein synthesis machinery. We have identified GSPT1 as a potential therapeutic vulnerability for MYC-driven cancers, including mCRPC. MRT-2359, our GSPT1-directed MGD, was designed to preferentially affect growth and survival of cancer cells addicted to protein translation, such as those driven by high expression and activity of MYC family transcription factors. Our preclinical studies showed that once-daily oral dosing of MRT-2359 led to potent antitumor activity in MYC-driven cell-line- and patient-derived xenograft models, and pointed to mCRPC as a potential indication for MRT-2359.

In December 2025, we announced positive interim data from an ongoing Phase 1/2 clinical study evaluating MRT-2359 in combination with enzalutamide in heavily pretreated patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). We provided further updates from this ongoing clinical study in February 2026, including at the ASCO Genitourinary Cancers Symposium held in San Francisco on February 26-28, 2026. In our February 2026 update we showed that in the subset of mCRPC patients with androgen receptor (AR) mutations, treatment with MRT-2359 in combination with enzalutamide led to a 100% PSA response rate in patients identified as having AR mutations (5 out of 5 patients). In addition, MRT-2359 plus enzalutamide demonstrated a 100% disease control rate in this patient subset, per RECIST criteria, including 2 RECIST partial responses and 3 with stable disease. In total, our study included 15 evaluable patients, including the 5 patients identified as having AR mutations. Across those 15 evaluable patients, the overall disease control rate was 67% (10 of 15), with 10 of 15 patients showing tumor size reductions of target lesions, including the 2 RECIST partial response patients that were also identified as having AR mutations.

Based on the success of our reported Phase 1/2 studies in mCRPC patients, we plan to initiate a Phase 2 study of MRT-2359 in combination with a second-generation AR inhibitor in mCRPC patients with AR mutations, with potential to expand the study into additional patient subsets, including patients naive to 2nd generation AR inhibitors. The study is anticipated to start in 2026.

paragraphs: Careful consideration should be given to the following risk factors, in addition to the other information set forth in this Annual Report and in other documents that we file with the SEC, in evaluating our business. Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. If any of the following risks and uncertainties actually occurs, our business, prospects, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. The risks described below are not intended to be exhaustive and are not the only risks that we face. New risk factors can emerge from time to time, and it is not possible to predict the impact that any factor or combination of factors may have on our business, prospects, financial condition and results of operations. Certain statements in this Annual Report are forward-looking statements. Please also see the section entitled "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements."

Biopharmaceutical drug development is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk. Since our formation as Monte Rosa Therapeutics AG in 2018, our operations have been limited primarily to organizing and staffing our company, business planning, raising capital, researching and developing our Quantitative and Engineered Elimination of Neosubstrates drug discovery engine, or our QuEENTM discovery engine, building our proprietary library of MGDs, developing our pipeline of product candidates, building our intellectual property portfolio, entering into collaboration agreements, undertaking preclinical and IND-enabling studies of our product candidates, and conducting our first clinical trials for MRT-2359, MRT-6160, and MRT-8102. We have never generated any revenue from drug sales. We have not obtained regulatory approvals for any of our current or future product candidates.

Typically, it takes many years to develop one new pharmaceutical drug from the time it is discovered to when it is available for treating patients. Consequently, any predictions we make about our future success or viability may not be as accurate as they could be if we had a longer operating history. In addition, as a business with a limited operating history, we may encounter unforeseen expenses, difficulties, complications, delays and other known and unknown factors, such as market volatility, public health crises or other geopolitical events. We will need to transition from a company focused on research and early-stage development to a company capable of supporting late-stage development and commercial activities. We may not be successful in such a transition.

Since our inception, we have focused substantially all of our efforts and financial resources on developing our proprietary QuEENTM discovery engine, our proprietary MGD library, and our initial pipeline of product candidates. To date, we have financed our operations primarily through the issuance and sale of convertible promissory notes and our convertible preferred stock to outside investors in private equity financings, public offerings of our common stock or warrants to purchase common stock, registered direct offerings, and our collaboration agreements with Roche and Novartis. From our inception through the date hereof, we raised an aggregate of $1.3 billion of gross proceeds from such transactions. As of December 31, 2025, our cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities were $382.1 million. We have incurred net losses in each year since our inception, and we had an accumulated deficit of $477.2 million as of December 31, 2025. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we reported net losses of $38.6 million and $72.7 million, respectively. Substantially all of our operating losses have resulted from costs incurred in connection with our research and initial pipeline programs and from general and administrative costs associated with our operations. We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and increasing operating losses over the next several years and for the foreseeable future. Our prior losses, combined with expected future losses, have had and will continue to have an adverse effect on our stockholders' deficit and working capital. We expect our expenses to significantly increase in connection with our ongoing activities, as we:
• conduct our clinical trial for MRT-2359, our MGD product candidate targeting GSPT1;
• finalize our Phase 1 clinical trial for MRT-8102, our NEK7-directed MGD being developed for the treatment of inflammatory conditions driven by the NLRP3 inflammasome, IL-1β, and IL-6;

paragraphs: You should read the following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations together with our consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This discussion contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties, including those described in the section titled "Special Note Regarding Forward Looking Statements." Our actual results and the timing of selected events could differ materially from those discussed below. Factors that could cause or contribute to such differences include, but are not limited to, those identified below and those set forth under the section titled "Risk Factors" included elsewhere in this Annual Report.

We are a biotechnology company developing a portfolio of novel and proprietary MGDs. MGDs are small molecule drugs that employ the body's natural protein destruction mechanisms to selectively degrade therapeutically relevant proteins. MGDs work by inducing the engagement of defined surfaces identified on target proteins by an E3 ligase, such as cereblon. We have developed a proprietary and industry-leading protein degradation discovery engine, called QuEENTM, to enable our unique and target-centric MGD discovery and development and our rational design of MGD products. We believe our small molecule MGDs may give us significant advantages over existing therapeutic modalities, including other protein degradation approaches. We prioritize our product development on therapeutic targets backed by strong biological and genetic rationale with the goal of discovering and developing novel medicines.

Monte Rosa Therapeutics AG, a Swiss operating company, was incorporated under the laws of Switzerland in April 2018. Monte Rosa Therapeutics, Inc. was incorporated in Delaware in November 2019. In 2020, through a common control reorganization, Monte Rosa Therapeutics, Inc. acquired the net assets and shareholding of Monte Rosa Therapeutics AG. Monte Rosa Therapeutics, Inc. includes wholly owned subsidiaries Monte Rosa Therapeutics AG and Monte Rosa Securities Corporation. We are headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts with research operations in both Boston and Basel, Switzerland.

To date, we have financed our operations primarily through the issuance and sale of convertible promissory notes, convertible preferred stock, public offerings of our common stock or warrants to purchase common stock, registered direct offerings, and through our collaboration agreements. From our inception through the date hereof, we raised an aggregate of $1.3 billion of gross proceeds from such transactions, inclusive of approximately $345 million gross proceeds raised through an underwritten public offering, or the 2026 Offering, subsequent to December 31, 2025, which is discussed in Note 16, Subsequent events, to our consolidated financial statements appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report.

Since inception, we have had significant operating losses. Our primary use of cash is to fund operating expenses, which consist primarily of research and development expenditures and, to a lesser extent, general and administrative expenditures. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we reported net losses of $38.6 million and $72.7 million, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $477.2 million and $382.1 million in cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and marketable securities. Aggregate net proceeds from the 2026 Offering were approximately $323.8 million after deducting the underwriter discounts, commissions, and other offering costs. We anticipate that our existing cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities, together with the proceeds from the 2026 Offering, defined below, supports our cash runway into 2029.

The development of our product candidates could be disrupted and materially adversely affected in the future by global economic or political developments. In addition, economic uncertainty in global markets caused by political instability and conflict, and economic challenges caused by global pandemics or other public health events, may lead to market disruptions, including significant volatility in commodity prices, credit and capital market instability and supply chain interruptions. Our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected by negative impacts on the global economy and capital markets resulting from these global economic conditions, particularly if such conditions are prolonged or worsen.

Collaboration revenue represents amounts earned from our collaboration and license agreements with Roche and Novartis. We expect that our revenue for the next several years will be derived primarily through our current collaboration and license agreements and any additional collaborations that we may enter into in the future.

In October 2023, Monte Rosa AG entered into a collaboration and license agreement, or the Roche Agreement, with Roche Basel and Roche US, and together with Roche Basel, Roche. Pursuant to the Roche Agreement, the parties will seek to identify MGDs against targets in cancer and neurological diseases selected by Roche using our proprietary drug discovery engine, where a certain number of targets selected by Roche are for a limited time subject to replacement rights owned by Roche. We will lead preclinical discovery and research activities with Roche leading late preclinical and clinical development activities.

Under the Roche Agreement, Roche will have a worldwide, exclusive license under patents and know-how controlled by us to develop and commercialize products directed to applicable targets. The license exclusivity is subject to our retained rights solely to fulfill our obligations under the arrangement.
The research collaboration activities governed by the Roche Agreement are overseen by a joint research committee.

In November 2023, we received a $50.0 million non-refundable upfront payment for the initial set of targets. Pursuant to the terms of the Roche Agreement, we expect to be entitled to receive from Roche certain variable consideration including potential preclinical milestones up to $172 million, and potential clinical, commercial and sales milestones exceeding $2 billion. We are also eligible to receive tiered royalties ranging from high-single-digit percent to low-teens percent on any products that are commercialized by Roche as a result of the collaboration.

Unless earlier terminated, the Roche Agreement will remain in effect for each product licensed under the Roche Agreement until expiration of the royalty term for the applicable product. The parties have included termination provisions in the Roche Agreement, allowing termination of the Roche Agreement in its entirety, on a country-by-country or a target-by-target basis.

In October 2024, Monte Rosa AG and Novartis entered into a license agreement with Novartis, or the 2024 Novartis Agreement. Pursuant to the 2024 Novartis Agreement, we granted to Novartis an exclusive, royalty-bearing, sublicensable and transferable license to develop, manufacture, and commercialize VAV1 MGDs, including MRT-6160. We were responsible for completing the Phase 1 clinical study and Novartis is responsible for all subsequent development and commercial activities starting at Phase 2. Development and commercial activities governed by the Novartis Agreement will be overseen by a Development Committee and a Commercialization Committee.

In December 2024, we received a $150 million non-refundable upfront payment. Pursuant to the 2024 Novartis Agreement, we are eligible to receive from Novartis up to $2.1 billion in development, regulatory, and sales milestones, beginning upon initiation of Phase 2 studies including (a) potential development and regulatory milestone payments, exceeding $1.5 billion if multiple indications achieve regulatory approval in multiple territories, (b) potential sales milestone payments in connection with sales outside of the U.S., and tiered royalties on sales outside of the U.S. Novartis will be responsible for costs associated with Phase 2 clinical studies. We and Novartis also agreed to a net profit and loss sharing arrangement prior to the initiation of Phase 3 clinical trials, pursuant to which we could co-fund any global clinical development from Phase 3 onwards and will share 30% of any profits and losses associated with the manufacturing and commercialization of the licensed products in the U.S. We have defined opportunities to opt out of the net profit and loss sharing arrangement. In such case, sales in the U.S. would be entitled to the potential sales milestone payments and tiered royalties as sales outside of the U.S. Any costs for any co-funded development and commercialization activities are subject to budgets reviewed by us and Novartis.

paragraphs: 本公司為一臨牀階段生技公司，開發具創新性及專屬知識財產之分子黏著降解劑（molecular glue degraders，簡稱 MGDs）。MGDs 為小分子藥物，利用人體自然的蛋白質分解機制，選擇性地降解具治療價值之蛋白質，實際上可編輯人類蛋白質組（proteome）。MGDs 透過誘導 E3 酪胺酸連接酶（如 cereblon）與目標蛋白質表面之特定結構特徵結合，來發揮作用。這些目標蛋白質亦稱為新底物（neosubstrates）。E3 酪胺酸連接酶隨後會透過添加一種稱為泛素（ubiquitin）之分子標記，標記目標蛋白質以進行降解。本公司相信，本公司之 MGDs 相較於現有治療方式，包括其他蛋白質降解方法，具有顯著優勢。
本公司已發展出一專屬且領先業界之發現引擎，稱為 QuEENTM（為「Quantitative and Engineered Elimination of Neosubstrates」之縮寫），以啟動本公司獨特之目標導向 MGD 發現與開發方法，以及本公司理性設計 MGD 產品候選品之方法。

截至目前為止，本公司之 QuEENTM 發現引擎已識別出許多可能被本公司 MGDs 目標之蛋白質，包括本公司產品候選品所針對之蛋白質。本公司結合人工智慧（AI）或機器學習（ML）引擎與多種專屬實驗工具，以識別適合被本公司 MGDs 降解之具治療價值之目標蛋白質。本公司持續增加對 MGDs 作用機制之理解，並運用此理解，開發設計新 MGDs 之設計原則。此成長之專業知識體現在本公司擴展之 MGD 庫以及發現與開發流程中。運用本公司之見解、知識與技術平台，本公司已產生一組 MGDs 庫，作為本公司 MGDs 程式之基礎。目前，本公司之庫包含一組多樣化之理性設計小分子，代表超過 1000 種獨特低分子量骨架，以及超過 75,000 種不同之 MGD 分子。本公司亦運用本公司之見解與學習成果，持續更新與改善 QuEENTM 以及本公司之 MGD 庫，持續提升發現引擎之效能。

本公司優先發展產品，以針對具強大生物與遺傳學理據之治療目標。本公司專注於開發解決臨牀重要適應症之方案，包括免疫學、發炎、心臟學、腫瘤學及其他適應症。截至目前為止，本公司之發現引擎已產生三個處於臨牀開發階段之計畫：MRT-6160，為針對 VAV1 之 MGD，用於免疫介導疾病；MRT-8102，為針對 NEK7 之 MGD，用於由 IL-1β、IL-6 與 NLRP3 炎症體驅動之發炎疾病；以及 MRT-2359，為針對 GSPT1 之 MGD，用於轉移性去勢抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）。

MRT-6160 是一種針對 VAV1 的 MGD，正在開發用於免疫相關疾病。我們的動物實驗顯示，透過 MGD 靶向降解 VAV1 蛋白質，可調節 T 細胞與 B 細胞受體的活動。我們的 VAV1 MGD，MRT-6160，在神經與全身性自身免疫及發炎疾病的動物模型中顯示出有前景的活性，因此我們認為其有潛力提供多重免疫相關疾病的治療效益，例如發炎性腸道疾病、類風濕性關節炎、皮膚疾患以及多發性硬化症。

於 2024 年 10 月，本公司宣佈與 Novartis 籤訂全球獨家開發與商業化授權協議，根據該協議，本公司授予 Novartis 獨家授權，用以開發、製造與商業化 VAV1 導向的 MGDs，包括 MRT-6160，起始為 Phase 2 臨牀研究。本公司自 Novartis 收到一筆 150 百萬美元的預付款，並有資格獲得最高達 2.1 十億美元的開發、監管及銷售里程碑付款，自 Phase 2 研究啟動開始，包括潛在的開發與監管里程碑付款，若多個適應症在多個地區獲得監管批准，付款金額可能超過 1.5 十億美元。本公司與 Novartis 並同意一項淨利潤與損失分享安排，根據該安排，本公司將共同資助 Phase 3 以後的全球臨牀開發，並將分享美國製造與商業化授權產品相關任何利潤與損失的 30%。本公司有資格從 Novartis 收到潛在的銷售里程碑付款及與美國以外銷售相關的階梯式版稅。本公司承擔已完成的 Phase 1 臨牀研究相關費用，而 Novartis 將承擔任何後續臨牀研究相關費用，除了根據利潤與損失分享協議由本公司承擔的 Phase 3 費用。

2025 年 3 月，我們宣佈 MRT-6160 的 Phase 1 研究的初步臨牀結果，顯示深層 VAV1 降解大於 90%，顯著的 T 細胞與 B 細胞功能抑制，包括對 T 細胞與 B 細胞 ex-vivo 發炎因子釋放的顯著抑制，以及整體良好的安全性與耐受性表現。我們認為這些數據支持進行多個 Phase 2 研究的明確路徑，並在免疫相關疾病中有廣泛的潛在應用。我們預期我們的合作夥伴 Novartis 將於 2026 年啟動多個 MRT-6160 在免疫相關疾病的 Phase 2 研究。

of cytokine release from T and B cells ex-vivo, and a generally favorable safety and tolerability profile. We believe these data support a clear path to multiple Phase 2 studies and broad potential applications in immune-mediated diseases. We expect that our collaborator, Novartis, will initiate multiple Phase 2 studies of MRT-6160 in immune-mediated diseases in 2026.

MRT-8102 是一種針對 NEK7 的 MGD，用以治療由 NLRP3 炎症小體、IL-1 與 IL-6 驅動的疾病與發炎性疾病。NLRP3 炎症小體是一種多蛋白質複合體，作為整合病原體、損傷與壓力訊號的中心節點，並觸發促發炎性細胞激素的產生。NLRP3 炎症小體異常活化與隨後釋放的活性白血球介素-1β（IL-1β）與白血球介素-18（IL-18）已被認為與多種發炎驅動的疾病有關，包括動脈粥狀硬化性心血管疾病（ASCVD）、痛風、hidradenitis suppurativa、心包炎、退化性關節炎與肥胖。NEK7 作為一種支架蛋白，以非絲胺酸蛋白激酶依賴方式促進 NLRP3 炎症小體的組裝與活化，這表示以 MGD 分子降解 NEK7 可能是一種預防 NLRP3 炎症小體活化與相關下游細胞激素產生的潛在治療方法。

2026 年 1 月，我們宣佈來自持續進行的第 1 期臨牀研究（現稱為 GFORCE-1）的初步正面數據，評估 MRT-8102。在心血管疾病（CVD）風險升高之受試者中，MRT-8102 顯示出快速且持續的系統性發炎減少。在 CVD 風險升高之受試者接受四週 MRT-8102 治療後，C-反應蛋白（CRP）水平下降了 85%，且 94% 的研究參與者達到 CRP 值低於 2 mg/L，這與降低 CVD 風險的門檻相關。單次遞增劑量（SAD）與多次遞增劑量（MAD）組別在 5 mg 到 400 mg 的劑量範圍內顯示出深層且持續的 NEK7 降解。觀察到良好的安全性，僅有輕度至中度不良事件（AEs），且無增加感染風險的證據。

我們持續進行的 GFORCE-1 研究，針對 CVD 風險升高之受試者評估 MRT-8102，已擴展至多個劑量層次，以加速 ASCVD 的發展。我們預期在 2026 年第二季取得此研究的結果。我們計畫在 2026 年第二季啟動一項 ASCVD 研究，GFORCE-2（針對 CVD 風險升高之患者，定義為第三期/第四期慢性腎臟病與 CRP 升高），在 2026 年第四季或 2027 年第一季啟動一項 MRT-8102 在痛風發作患者的第二期研究，GFORCE-3，以及在 2027 年第一季啟動一項 MRT-8102 在 hidradenitis suppurativa 患者中的第二期研究，GFORCE-4。此外，我們預期在 2026 年提交一項針對下一代 NEK7 導向 MGD 的 IND 申請。

MRT-2359 是一種口服生物可利用的 MGD，針對翻譯終止因子蛋白 GSPT1，目前處於臨牀開發階段，潛在用於 MYC 驅動的腫瘤，特別是轉移性荷爾蒙抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）。GSPT1（也稱為 eRF3a）是一種翻譯終止因子，幫助催化蛋白質合成的終止，促進 mRNA 與新合成蛋白質從核糖體蛋白合成機制中釋放。我們已將 GSPT1 識別為 MYC 驅動癌症的潛在治療弱點，包括 mCRPC。MRT-2359，我們的 GSPT1 導向 MGD，是設計用以選擇性影響依賴蛋白質翻譯的癌細胞生長與存活，例如那些由高表達與活動的 MYC 家族轉錄因子驅動的癌細胞。我們的預臨牀研究顯示，每日一次口服 MRT-2359 治療在 MYC 驅動的細胞株與患者衍生異體移植模型中顯示出強效的抗腫瘤活性，並指出 mCRPC 可能是 MRT-2359 的潛在適應症。

2025 年 12 月，我們宣佈來自持續進行的第 1 期/第 2 期臨牀研究的初步正面數據，評估 MRT-2359 與 enzalutamide 組合在多重治療後的轉移性荷爾蒙抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）患者中的效果。我們在 2026 年 2 月進一步更新了此持續臨牀研究的數據，包括在 2026 年 2 月 26 日至 28 日於舊金山舉行的 ASCO 泌尿系統癌症學會上發表的資料。在 2026 年 2 月的更新中，我們顯示在具有雄激素受體（AR）突變的 mCRPC 患者子羣中，MRT-2359 與 enzalutamide 組合治療使具有 AR 突變的患者（共 5 位患者）達到 100% 的 PSA 回應率。此外，MRT-2359 與 enzalutamide 在此患者子羣中顯示出 100% 的疾病控制率，根據 RECIST 標準，包括 2 例 RECIST 部分反應與 3 例穩定疾病。總體而言，我們的研究包含 15 位可評估患者，包括 5 位被識別為具有 AR 突變的患者。在這 15 位可評估患者中，總體疾病控制率為 67%（10 位患者），其中 10 位患者顯示目標病竈的腫瘤大小減少，包括 2 位 RECIST 部分反應患者，他們也被識別為具有 AR 突變。
基於我們報告的 mCRPC 患者第 1 期/第 2 期研究的成功，我們計畫在 2026 年啟動一項 MRT-2359 與第二代 AR 抑製劑組合的第 2 期研究，針對具有 AR 突變的 mCRPC 患者，並有潛力將研究擴展至其他患者子羣，包括未接觸過第二代 AR 抑製劑的患者。此研究預計於 2026 年啟動。

paragraphs: 你應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與我們合併財務報表及相關附註一同審閱。本討論包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性，包括在「特別聲明前瞻性陳述」一節中所描述的風險。我們實際的結果及部分事件的時間點可能與下列討論有重大差異。導致這種差異的因素包括，但不限於下列所列及在本年度報告「風險因素」一節中所列的風險因素。

我們是一家生物技術公司，正在開發一系列新型且專有的MGDs。MGDs是小分子藥物，利用身體的自然蛋白分解機制，選擇性地降解治療相關的蛋白質。MGDs透過誘導E3泛素連接酶（例如cereblon）與目標蛋白質上特定表面的結合而發揮作用。我們已開發出專屬且領先業界的蛋白質降解發現引擎，稱為QuEENTM，以實現我們獨特且以目標為中心的MGDs發現與開發，以及我們對MGDs產品的理性設計。我們相信我們的小分子MGDs可能在現有治療方式，包括其他蛋白質降解方法上，提供我們顯著的優勢。我們優先發展具有強大生物與遺傳理據的治療目標，目標為發現與開發新型藥物。

Monte Rosa Therapeutics AG為一家瑞士營運公司，於2018年4月根據瑞士法律設立。Monte Rosa Therapeutics, Inc.於2019年11月根據特拉華州法律設立。2020年，透過共同控制重組，Monte Rosa Therapeutics, Inc.取得Monte Rosa Therapeutics AG的淨資產與股權。Monte Rosa Therapeutics, Inc.包含 wholly owned subsidiaries Monte Rosa Therapeutics AG與Monte Rosa Securities Corporation。我們的總部設於馬薩諸塞州波士頓，研究作業則在波士頓與瑞士巴塞爾進行。
截至目前為止，我們主要透過發行與銷售可轉換期票、可轉換優先股、公開發行我們的普通股或購買普通股的認購權證、註冊直接發行，以及透過合作協議來資助營運。從我們成立至本報告日，我們透過這些交易共籌得約1.3十億美元的總資金，包含約345百萬美元的總資金來自於2026年公開發行（即2026年發行），該發行是在2025年12月31日之後進行，並在本年度報告的財務報表附註16「後續事件」中討論。

我們產品候選藥物的開發可能因全球經濟或政治發展而受到幹擾，並在未來產生重大不利影響。此外，由政治不穩定與衝突所導致的全球市場經濟不確定性，以及由全球疫情或其他公共衛生事件所造成的經濟挑戰，可能導致市場動盪，包括商品價格的重大波動、信貸與資本市場的不穩定，以及供應鏈中斷。我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果可能因這些全球經濟條件對全球經濟與資本市場造成的負面影響而產生重大且不利的影響，特別是如果這些條件持續或惡化的情況下。
合作收入代表我們透過與Roche及Novartis的合作與授權協議所賺取的金額。我們預期未來幾年的收入主要來自我們目前的合作與授權協議，以及我們未來可能簽訂的任何其他合作協議。

2023年10月，Monte Rosa AG與Roche Basel及Roche US簽訂了一項合作與授權協議（即Roche協議），並與Roche Basel共同與Roche合作。根據Roche協議，雙方將尋求針對Roche所選的癌症與神經疾病目標，利用我們的專屬藥物發現引擎尋找MGDs，其中Roche所選的目標中，某些目標在有限時間內可能受到Roche的替換權所限制。我們將領導預臨牀發現與研究活動，而Roche將領導晚期預臨牀與臨牀開發活動。
根據 Roche 合約，Roche 將擁有全球獨家授權，根據我們控制的專利及知識產權，開發及商業化針對適用目標的產品。此授權獨佔性受限於我們保留的權利，僅用以履行根據協議的義務。
根據 Roche 合約規範的研發合作活動，由聯合研發委員會監督。

2023 年 11 月，我們收到一筆 50.0 百萬美元的不可退預付款，用以針對初始目標組。根據 Roche 合約條款，我們預期將從 Roche 獲得某些變動性報酬，包括潛在的前期臨牀里程碑報酬，最高達 172 百萬美元，以及潛在的臨牀、商業及銷售里程碑報酬，總計超過 2 十億美元。我們也有資格根據任何因合作而由 Roche 開發商業化的產品，獲得階梯式版稅，範圍為高單數位百分比至低 teens 百分比。
除非較早終止，Roche 合約將對每個根據 Roche 合約授權的產品持續生效，直至適用產品的版稅期限屆滿。雙方已在 Roche 合約中包含終止條款，允許根據國家或目標，終止 Roche 合約的全部內容。

2024 年 10 月，Monte Rosa AG 與 Novartis 籤訂了一項授權協議，稱為 2024 Novartis 合約。根據 2024 Novartis 合約，我們授予 Novartis 獨家、可收取版稅、可再授權及可轉讓的授權，用以開發、製造及商業化 VAV1 MGDs，包括 MRT-6160。我們負責完成第一期臨牀研究，而 Novartis 則負責所有後續的開發及商業活動，從第二期臨牀研究開始。根據 Novartis 合約規範的開發及商業活動，將由開發委員會及商業化委員會監督。

2024 年 12 月，我們收到一筆 150 百萬美元的不可退預付款。根據 2024 Novartis 合約，我們有資格從 Novartis 獲得最高達 2.1 十億美元的開發、法規及銷售里程碑報酬，自第二期研究啟動時開始，包括 (a) 潛在的開發及法規里程碑報酬，若多個適應症在多個地區獲得法規批准，總計可能超過 1.5 十億美元，(b) 潛在的銷售里程碑報酬，與銷售於美國以外地區有關，以及美國以外地區銷售的階梯式版稅。Novartis 將負責第二期臨牀研究的相關費用。我們與 Novartis 也同意在第三期臨牀試驗啟動前，進行淨利潤與損失分享安排，根據此安排，我們可共同資助任何全球臨牀開發，從第三期開始，並將分享美國製造及商業化授權產品的任何利潤與損失的 30%。我們已定義了退出淨利潤與損失分享安排的機會。在此情況下，美國銷售將有資格獲得與美國以外銷售相同的潛在銷售里程碑報酬及階梯式版稅。任何共同資助的開發及商業化活動的費用，將根據我們與 Novartis 審查的預算進行管理。

headings: 與本公司財務狀況及資金需求相關之風險
本公司為一家生物科技公司，營運歷史有限，截至目前為止尚未自藥品銷售中產生任何收入，且可能永遠無法實現盈利。
自本公司成立以來，我們已產生重大營運虧損，並預期在可預見的未來，我們將持續產生虧損。
與本公司業務及產業相關之風險
我們可能尋求並未能取得美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）對我們現有或未來產品候選藥物之突破性療法指定（Breakthrough Therapy Designation）或加速審批指定（Fast Track Designation）
paragraphs: 應謹慎考量下列風險因素，除本年度年報及其他本公司向 SEC 提交之文件中所載之資訊外，評估本公司業務。投資本公司普通股涉及高度風險。若下列任何風險與不確定性實際發生，將可能對本公司業務、前景、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。下列所描述之風險並非完整列出，亦非本公司所面臨之唯一風險。隨時間推移，可能出現新風險因素，且無法預測任何因素或因素組合對本公司業務、前景、財務狀況及營運成果可能產生之影響。本年度年報中某些陳述為前瞻性陳述。請同時參閱「關於前瞻性陳述之特別說明」一節。

生技藥物開發為極具風險且高度投機性之工作，涉及相當程度之風險。自 2018 年成立 Monte Rosa Therapeutics AG 以來，本公司業務主要限於組織與僱用員工、業務規劃、籌措資金、研究與開發我們之 Quantitative and Engineered Elimination of Neosubstrates 藥物發現引擎，或稱 QuEENTM 發現引擎、建立我們之專屬 MGD 組合、開發我們之產品候選藥物管線、建立我們之智慧財產權組合、簽訂合作協議、進行我們產品候選藥物之臨牀前及 IND 啓動研究，以及進行我們 MRT-2359、MRT-6160 及 MRT-8102 之首次臨牀試驗。本公司從未自藥物銷售中產生任何收入。本公司尚未取得任何現有或未來產品候選藥物之監管核准。

通常，從藥物被發現至可供用於治療病患，需耗費許多年時間。因此，我們對未來成功或存續性所做的預測，可能不如我們有較長營運歷史時所做出的預測準確。此外，作為一家營運歷史有限之公司，我們可能遭遇預期之外之費用、困難、複雜問題、延誤及其他已知或未知因素，例如市場波動、公共衛生危機或其他地緣政治事件。我們將需要從專注於研究與早期階段開發之公司，轉型為能支持晚期階段開發與商業活動之公司。我們可能無法成功進行此轉型。

自成立以來，本公司已將大部分努力與財務資源投入於開發我們之專屬 QuEENTM 發現引擎、專屬 MGD 組合及初始產品候選藥物管線。截至目前為止，本公司主要透過發行及銷售可轉換票據與可轉換優先股至外部投資者，進行私人股權融資、公開發行普通股或發行認購普通股權證、註冊直接發行，以及與 Roche 及 Novartis 之合作協議來籌措營運資金。自成立至本文件簽署日為止，本公司透過上述交易共籌得 1.3 十億美元之總資金。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司之現金、現金等價物、限制性現金及市場可交易證券為 382.1 百萬美元。自成立以來，本公司每年均產生淨虧損，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司累積虧損為 477.2 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日，本公司分別報告淨虧損為 38.6 百萬美元及 72.7 百萬美元。本公司幾乎所有營運虧損均來自與研究及初始管線計畫相關之費用，以及與營運相關之總務及行政費用。本公司預期在未來數年及可預見之未來，持續產生重大費用及增加之營運虧損。本公司過去之虧損，加上預期未來之虧損，已對股東權益及營運資金造成不利影響，並將持續造成不利影響。本公司預期因進行持續活動，費用將大幅增加，包括：
• 進行 MRT-2359 之臨牀試驗，此為針對 GSPT1 之 MGD 產品候選藥物；
• 完成 MRT-8102 之 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，此為針對 NEK7 之 MGD，用於治療由 NLRP3 炎症小體、IL-1β 及 IL-6 驅動之發炎性疾病。
